newsitem.title: UK: UK's Harrods owner Al Fayed buys into Fulham FC.
newsitem.headline: UK's Harrods owner Al Fayed buys into Fulham FC.

text.p: Mohamed Al Fayed, the owner of luxury London department store Harrods, has agreed to become the major shareholder in English second division soccer club Fulham, Harrods said on Thursday.

Egyptian-born businessman Al Fayed will become club chairman as part of the deal while the club has re-acquired the freehold to its Craven Cottage stadium on the banks of the river Thames in west London.
The new owners have promised substantial investment to acquire players and improve and develop a stadium which the club has occupied for a century.

Craven Cottage is only a few minutes' drive from the world renowned Harrods store in Knightsbridge. Al Fayed is reported to be planning to add shops and restaurants as part of the redevelopment of the stadium.
The financing for future investments will come from Al Fayed's Fulham Leisure Holdings company and the Muddyman family, the other main shareholders.

Al Fayed promised to work to restore the fortunes of Fulham, a club which has spent most of its existence in the lower divisions of the English game. Fulham were recently promoted from the third division, the bottom rung on the professional ladder.
"I am totally committed, both personally and financially, to the plans for the revival of the club and I look forward to sharing a bright future with the loyal fans," he said in a statement.
